DECISION_RULE_precommitted_by_PI.small_e_q_everywhere: waypoint quantization is probably not the main bottleneck -> proceed to macro-adapter audit and privileged-vs-standard BC
DECISION_RULE_precommitted_by_PI.large_e_q_for_GUARD_at_4v4_6v6: the ACTION interface is likely part of the scaling defect -> do NOT design BC as though observation is the only difference
DECISION_RULE_precommitted_by_PI.large_e_q_even_at_2v2: PAUSE -- the action projection may not faithfully represent even the WORKING strategy
DECISION_RULE_precommitted_by_PI.BREACH_small_GUARD_large: particularly compelling: it matches the exact strategic component that is causing trouble

INVALIDATION.why: e_q was computed as if EVERY teacher target had to be expressed through the 50-waypoint GO_TO head. It does not. gpu_env/_core/_rules.py::_build_targets_from_action resolves GET_FLAG to the EXACT enemy flag position and GO_HOME to the EXACT own flag home, bypassing the waypoint vocabulary entirely; a carrying agent is also redirected to exact home. BREACH's target is always the enemy flag and GUARD's defender default is always home, so this metric charged the student a quantization cost it never pays.
INVALIDATION.the_tell: median e_q was identical at 2.076 in all six cells. That is not a measurement, it is the fixed distance from flag/home to the nearest waypoint.
INVALIDATION.would_have_caused: the reported >1-cell fractions of 0.86-0.97 INCLUDING at 2v2 would have triggered the PI's 'large e_q even at 2v2 -> PAUSE' branch and sent us toward redesigning the action space for the wrong reason.
INVALIDATION.superseded_by: conditional e_q computed only on the GO_TO branch (see ARM1_MACRO_ADAPTER_AUDIT when frozen)
INVALIDATION.retained_because: the failure mode is worth preserving: a metric must be conditioned on the actual execution pathway, not on an assumed one.
